name: Battery ignition
summary: A battery shorted through fine steel wool or a wire — the fastest fire in the corpus if you happen to be carrying a dead torch.

materials.item: fine steel wool or thin wire

steps.text: Tease the steel wool out into a loose, airy pad and nest it in the tinder bundle BEFORE you touch it to anything.
9V: press both terminals directly onto the wool. It lights instantly.
AA/AAA: run a short length of wire, or a foil strip cut narrow in the middle, from + to −. The narrow waist is where it heats.
steps.why: The thin section has the highest resistance, so that is where the heat concentrates. A uniformly wide strip just gets warm and drains the cell.

steps.text: Steel wool burns fast and hot but briefly — blow gently and feed it fine tinder immediately.
A LITHIUM phone or power-bank cell will do this too, and violently. Treat it as a last resort, not a technique.

verify: The wool glows orange and the glow spreads on its own. If it only warms, the wool is too coarse or the cell is too flat.
limits: It burns out in seconds — this is an ignition source, not a fire. Without prepared tinder underneath it you get a bright flash and nothing.
It depends entirely on carrying the right two manufactured things. It is the top of the ladder, not the bottom.
Coarse steel wool (the kind in a kitchen) works poorly. It wants the fine grade.
cautions: PUNCTURING OR SHORTING A LITHIUM CELL can cause a vent-with-flame and toxic smoke, and it is not controllable once started. Do it outdoors, downwind, and never in a shelter or a pack.
Steel wool in a pack beside a battery is a fire waiting to happen. Store them apart — this has burned through rucksacks.
A shorted battery gets hot enough to burn your hand.
